scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Dwell magazine, modern-architecture spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad X2D 100C, XCD 45mm f/2.8, aperture f/4. A poured-concrete residential staircase at night, treads cantilevered from a raw plaster wall. A small square frameless COB recessed step light sits flush into the baseboard at ankle height, its face barely distinguishable from the surrounding wall finish — one modest glowing rectangle among shadow. The fixture matches the variant reference image exactly — finish and form as shown. Concrete shows hairline shrinkage cracks and a faint dust film along the tread nosings; the plaster wall carries a ghost watermark near the base. Exposure committed: the lit tread edge clips to near-white, upper stair run stays genuinely dark — no fill, no artificial balance. Warm 3000K glow stays strictly local, cool ambient from a distant skylight stays cool, no blending. Kodak Portra 400 grain throughout, 2% corner vignette, 1px chromatic aberration at the clipped tread edge. Palette: raw concrete grey, warm ivory plaster, shadow black, clipped chalk-white, dusty taupe. No people, no alcohol.
scenes.cameraAngle: low three-quarter, ankle level looking up the stair run

Exposure committed: the lit tread clips hard, the stair descent below falls to near-black — no bounce fill. Cool 4000K source stays local and neutral; no warm cast introduced.
